leftEvidence.role: The baptism becomes a public question
leftEvidence.title: Jesus asks leaders to judge John’s baptism

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: When leaders challenge Jesus’ authority, he asks whether John’s baptism came from heaven or humans.
points.right: Chief priests, scribes, and elders ask by what authority Jesus acts; he answers with a question about John’s baptism.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Their public calculation prevents an answer; Jesus then tells of two sons and recalls that they did not believe John.
points.right: They reason about heaven, unbelief, and fear of the crowd, then say they do not know.

payload.posture: Both witnesses preserve Jesus’ counterquestion and the leaders’ calculation.

rightEvidence.role: The baptism becomes a public question
rightEvidence.title: Mark links Jesus’ authority question to John’s baptism

payload.tension: Matthew extends the exchange with the two sons and unbelief after seeing others respond.
payload.title: John’s baptism in two authority disputes
